title: Agreement opens via ordinary etale restriction
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a sheaf of sets on its small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], $Q$ an étale object over $S$, and $s,t\in F(Q)$. There exists an open $E\subset Q$ such that, for every étale object $A/S$ and morphism $m:A\to Q$ over $S$, $\operatorname{range}(m)\subset E$ if and only if $F(m)(s)=F(m)(t)$. Here restriction is the ordinary presheaf map on the small étale site, not an untyped inverse-image identification.

source.place: Tag 09XM (lemma-where-sections-are-equal), specialized to etale test objects; Tag 03S2 restriction identification

proof.text: Take the canonical agreement open from Tag 09XM. For an etale test object A, m.left composed with Q.hom is A.hom. Use canonicalSection_eq_iff to substitute this structure map without dependent rewriting. The restriction isomorphism for A.hom, evaluated at its identity object, is injective. Its naturality and its counit/unit formula send the canonical restriction of each section to its ordinary restriction along m followed by the isomorphism from that identity object to A. That last map is also injective. Hence canonical equality is equivalent to ordinary equality. Factorization through E is equivalent to range containment by the open immersion lift and its pointwise inclusion formula.

theorem exists_etaleSections_equal_open_etale_criterion
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (F : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (Q : S.Etale) (s t : F.obj.obj (op Q)) :
    ∃ E : Q.left.Opens, ∀ (A : S.Etale) (m : A ⟶ Q),
      Set.range m.left ⊆ (E : Set Q.left) ↔ F.obj.map m.op s = F.obj.map m.op t
